newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk contractors say Libya to pay part of debts.
newsitem.headline: Turk contractors say Libya to pay part of debts.

text.p: Turkish contractors said on Friday Libya would make a first payment on $350 million in outstanding debts next Monday after intense talks by officials of the two countries.
"Libya will pay an initial $40 million on Monday to the (Turkey-based) Arap-Turk Bank," said Kadir Sever, head of the Turkish Contractors' Association.

He said "bureaucratic obstacles on the part of the Libyan government" which delayed the payment since Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's visit to the North African country last month had been removed.
Libya owns about $350 million to Turkish contracting companies, which have completed 257 infrastructure projects worth $8.6 billion there since the 1970s.
An agreement between the two countries in 1994 made $120 million of the outstanding debt payable in equal installments, but Libya had failed to pay them.
